notes.title: Gamescom Round Up
notes.content:
Hello Trip Tenders!

What a launch week! We showcased Tempest Tower at Gamescom as part of the Indie Arena Booth, and loved every second of it. Seeing players engage with Tempest Tower and chatting with fans was such a wholesome experience. We event had a line!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45156611/8f20e84467e696417d889def953b58ec971ce54a.jpg

Thank you for buying Tempest Tower
Thank you to everyone who joined us on this journey through Early Access and to everyone who bought the game in this last week. It means the world to us to see people enjoying Tempest Tower. Self-publishing was a brand new experience for us and the response we have gotten from our community has been incredibly rewarding. We hope you continue to enjoy Tempest Tower, and that you keep an eye out for the next Half Past Yellow game (whenever it comes).

Remember to Review
If you haven't already, we would really appreciate you leaving a review for the game. It helps a lot with discovery and lets players know what to expect from the game before they buy. Thanks in advance!

Bundle with Sulfur
We are also exicted to be bundled up with Sulfur, an amazing FPS Roguelike made by our friends over at Perfect Random. If you thrive in the hectic action phases seen in the later levels of Tempest Tower and yearn for old-school shooter gameplay, then Sulfur is probably for you.

https://store.steampowered.com/bundle/58303/SULFUR_x_Tempest_Tower/
Future Plans
Our trip to Gamescom wasn't all about showcasing. We also had meetings with potential porting studios for Tempest Tower. We don't have anything to report just yet, but we would love to see the game on consoles and we are working to make it a reality.

In terms of future content updates, we have nothing to report at the moment. We will be keeping a close eye on player feedback and providing hotfixes for any glaring issues that the community discovers in the game. If you have any feedback for us, feel free to post in the Community Hub or join our Discord.

Gamescom - Player Stats
As mentioned above, we had a lot of fun showcasing Tempest Tower at Gamescom this year. If you didn't get a chance to go to the event, you can absorb some of the experience through the Steam Event (and this news post).

It was our first time showcasing a game at Gamescom and we were so proud to be a part of the Indie Arena Booth alongside so many other awesome indies! Over 200 people played Tempest Tower and we thought it would be fun to share some of the stats from the show:

Total Jumps - 49,045
Total Gusts - 69,287
Total Deaths - 462 (an average of about 2 per person)
Enemies Killed - 265,042 (which is crazy)
Enemies Stomped - 9,837
Waves Cleared - 877
Victories - 205 
Buildings Placed - 13,503
Souls Collected - 108,304

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45156611/75836282c0d2e72782cb3c49d98c3ced5e24f1c5.jpg

Pitch Please!
One of the main highlights from Gamescom was participating in the Indie Arena Booth Livestream. Max and Terri had 90 seconds to pitch Tempest Tower to a panel of judges and they knocked it out of the park! Tempest Tower was selected for a 30 minute showcase on the Indie Arena Livestream 🎉
You can check out the Half Past Yellow pitch strategy below and let us know what you think!

[previewyoutube=rkbyWzRB0Dk;full][/previewyoutube]

Other cool Tower Defense games!
Tempest Tower wasn't the only Tower Defense game that was being shown off at the Indie Arena Booth this year. One of the many awesome indie games that we saw in the Indie Arena Booth was Monuments to Ruin. A Roguelite Tower Defense with a really interesting exploration/fog mechanic and a vast advancements tree that looks very fun to explore.
If that sounds like your kind of Tower Defense, then you can check it out here!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/3579410/Monuments_to_Ruin/

Another cool TD game that caught our eye was Dawn of Defense. It offers a fantastic mix of Tower Defense and RTS elements, all wrapped up in a roguelike structure. Build towers to fight enemy troops in the trenches, train warriors to retake territory on the high ground. Reclaim your lands and defeat the baneful Empire! 
Check out the game right here on Steam to learn more!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2781660/Dawn_Of_Defense/

notes.title: Post 1.0 Fixes
notes.content:
Hello Trip Tenders,

We have a bigger "Post Launch" news post coming tomorrow that covers a bunch of things from Gamescom to future plans. Today we have a small patch that resolves a couple of recurring problems we saw at the showcase.

Patch Notes

Removed a rogue enemy spawn point in Tutorial - Wave 3
Updated Fuel placement in the Tutorial
Added a particle effect to the Tower Switch in Tutorial - Wave 1 to better guide players
Spike Trap description no longer says "Jump to activate" (this was an English only issue)
Dynamo Switch no longer says "Gust to activate" in all languages except English
Increased Peeper collection radius when herding Peepers back to the Tower

Gamepad Control Updates

A can now be used to select in the build menu
Right Trigger can be used to pick up and drop items
Left Trigger can be used to open the build menu in build mode
These are all additional controls to improve playability on the gamepad, the general control scheme remains unchanged. Tutorial prompts still direct players to the same controls.

notes.title: MAJOR UPDATE 02 - Level Challenges!
notes.content:
Hello Trip Tenders!

Today we have a brand new content update for you, plus news on Tempest Tower 1.0 👀 Take a look and let us know what you think.

About the Update
We have 3 big additions this update; Level Challenges, Stat Tracking, and a bunch of new Upgrades. If you ever wanted to recover health by stomping on enemies or transform your Dynamo Switch into an AOE lightning machine, then this is the update for you!

Level Challenges
Completing a level in Tempest Tower is now only the begining. To truly master a level, you must complete all three challenges:

Save every Peeper
End the level with zero Tower Damage
Clear all Noxious Goop

These challenges can be completed in isolation, ticking them off one by one, or you can try and take out multiple in one go. Each challenge you clear will upgrade the Trophy displayed by that level portal. Can you get the elusive Platinum Trophy on every level of the game?!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45156611/9e47b7a54f657aec5d5d4b20c8048f69dd13d220.gif

Stat Tracking
If you like seeing arbitrary numbers go up then you will want to check in on the Player Stat Screen after every level. We added the tracking to create more interesting achievements, then realised it was also be fun to just see some of these numbers exposed at all times. Unfortunately, we weren't tracking the data before this update so everything will start at zero, but we hope you enjoy seeing this going forward.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45156611/da581f42bd89e6a83940f13c048cd7bb7b7fca0f.jpg

New Upgrades
The Level Challenges Update also adds 21 new Upgrades to the game. The upgrades focus mostly on making your buildings more effective, but there are a couple of player upgrades as well. Save as many Peepers as possible to make the best use of all these new options!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45156611/4c588624ac2668ef16b39d4068eea046f728c4c4.gif

Roadmap to 1.0
Tempest Tower will leave Early Access on August 19th at 10am Pacific Time! The 1.0 update will bring new levels, enemies, buildings, and more. We are so excited to fully release Tempest Tower, check out the updated roadmap for more info.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45156611/2cbe8ef0d8e6d340a510fa1f5dc3a1a641537a87.png

Gamescom 2025
If you will be at Gamescom in August, then come say hi to us at the Indie Arena Booth in Hall 10.2! You will be able to play the 1.0 version of Tempest Tower and compete for the Gamescom highscore. We are so excited to be showcasing Tempest Tower next to so many other awesome indie games. It will be our first time showcasing at such a large event and we can't wait to see what that is like 🎉

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45156611/96c1be3a771a50f89e6f83e8eb82eb950842a369.jpg

Patch Notes - v0.82
Levels and Worlds

Added Level Challenges
Added a Trophy Display to show the completion state of each level
Added a player stat screen to the Hub


Upgrades

21 new draftable upgrades
Added rarity system to Upgrade Cards
Removed Bomb Bounce upgrade as it was too powerful (Super Stomp has been created to replace the effect)


Meta

Added player stat tracking (levels completed, number of deaths, jumps, etc.)

notes.content:
Hello Trip Tenders!

We have just launched the first Major Update for Tempest Tower as part of the Best Indie Games Summer Showcase 2025 🎉

I hope you are ready to touch some grass, because this update brings you to a brand new world: The Garden. The Garden world features a new enemy type to deal with as well as new hazards and items.

We think that this new world space adds a boatload of charm to the game and we will be expanding on this space as we go.

You can see the trailer for the Touch Grass Update right here!

notes.title: First Update: Difficulty Tweaks
notes.content:
Hi everybody!

Tempest Tower is almost 14 days old and we have been collating a lot of early feedback. Many players feel that the difficulty curve of the game is quite steep and unforgiving, and this is reflected in the median time played. To combat this, we have made some balance changes, added a new level, and updated the experience required to unlock new buildings. We hope that this update smooths out the difficulty curve, while still offering a challenge in the later levels.

Last chance to get Tempest Tower at 10% off
The Tempest Tower launch discount is ending on Monday! The weekend is the perfect time to grab the game if you think it is for you.

Full Patch Notes

New Level: added an easier level after the tutorial to help with initial player experience
Updated Level Order: level order has been shifted to accomodate for this new level (for example "Desert World 4" is now "Desert World 5")
Level Balance: general balance/difficulty tweaks across all levels 
Rework of enemy navigation to be more robust and performant 
Additional decorative objects placed around levels (sandcastles!)

notes.title: The Gentle Art of Making Enemies
notes.content:
The element of our game Tempest Tower that we get asked about the most on social media is the art style. Specifically, the visual style of our enemies. There just seems to be something in how they look, fans repeatedly asked how we are achieving such a “crisp” and sometimes “clayish” look. Today we are diving into exactly that.

Return of the Lost Peepers
Meet the Peepers – the endearing little eyeball creatures that inhabit the world of Tempest Tower, and a kind of representation of consciousness. They always seem a little lost and “in over their eyes,” like they need a little help to cross the road or figure out where they’re going.

These little guys were looking for guidance in a previous, unfinished project. We liked them too much to leave them behind and felt they deserved the spotlight (and maybe the rescue!) they never truly received.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45156611/8d637426e8318f67e804ecde330b9b09c15aba7a.png

Creepers: Crafting the Anti-Peeper
As Tempest Tower is a tower defense game, enemies are essential. Lots of them. Our first concept was a direct counterpoint to our vulnerable Peepers: the Anti-Peeper. If Peepers represent consciousness, these enemies would embody its absence: hollow, vacant-eyed beings acting without clear intent.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45156611/a5c86e75d26e84ff88d51ed6bbf74bbce3b42023.png

To learn more about how the design of the default Creeper evolved and new designs were introduced. You should check out the Guest Blog we wrote for Unity. There are some cool videos as well as a description of the shader magic we are using to make the Creepers look so good! You can read the full blog here!

Happy day after release!
We are getting such great feedback on Tempest Tower at the moment and we are so excited to see that players are enjoying the game! We are taking all the initial feedback we hear into consideration and we will have a proper post launch news post at the end of the week!

Until then, don't forget to check out all the great games featured in the Nordic Game Sale!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45156611/34333a4135901931993fcab54168c5c62c3f4ac7.png

notes.title: Tempest Tower - Out Now!
notes.content:
Today is the day! Tempest Tower is out now on Steam Early Access. We are so excited to see what you think of the game and to continue to refine it alongside the community. 
We are collecting feedback (and bug reports 😬) via the Steam Community Hub and over on the Half Past Yellow Discord Server. For bugs, it would be helpful if you used the Mega Thread, as it is easier for us to keep track of things as they come up.

An Early Access Game
Tempest Tower is the first game we have ever released via Early Access. It is a strange feeling for us, because the game isn't finished yet. For better, or for worse, the previous games we have released as a studio didn't launch with planned updates or ongoing development in mind.
We are looking forward to trying something new with Tempest Tower and we have spent the last 6 months learning as much as we could about making a great Early Access game. The Half Past Yellow team are proud what Tempest Tower is today, but we also know that the game will improve so much over this Early Access period. We hope that you will join us on this journey to build a game that everyone in the community is proud of.

Today Tempest Tower contains:

 A Tutorial + 4 Levels
 14 Towers
 28 Draftable Upgrades
 2-3 hours of core playtime (+ endless replayable fun)

Got Questions? Check the FAQ
We have pinned a Tempest Tower FAQ in the Discussion tab of the Community HUB. We will keep it up to date as more questions are asked frequently.

Development Roadmap
While Tempest Tower is in Early Access, we will publish roadmap updates as we add new content to the game so you are always aware of upcoming changes to Tempest Tower. Take a look!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45156611/c6ce43d8d818f599d803a8106e666bc3872d8229.png

A Half Past Yellow Bundle
Tempest Tower is Half Past Yellow's second commercial game (if you want to see some of our less commercial titles you can take a look at our itch page). To celebrate this we have created a Tempest Tower x Time on Frog Island bundle, so if you haven't tried ToFI yet, then there has never been a better time to start your island hopping adventure! Check it out here.

Beyond that though, we are so proud of how Tempest Tower plays, looks, and sounds, so we hope that you can look past the menu interface and try out the game.

We want your feedback!
Tempest Tower is an Early Access title so the sooner we start gathering real world feedback the better. If you have any suggestions, feedback, or bug/crash reports you can get them to us via the Community Hub or our Discord. 
We will have a Mega Thread in the Community Hub for bug reporting as this is the easiest way for us to keep track of different issues. Beyond that, starting individual threads for feedback and gameplay suggestions is the best way to engage with us and have your thoughts considered.

Everyone on the Half Past Yellow team is eager to hear what you think of Tempest Tower. I hope you enjoy your time with the Demo and keep an eye out for the full release SOON 👀

notes.title: Introducing Fai
notes.content:
We had a few questions come up on our Discord about the main character of Tempest Tower and their role in the world of Trip Space. It’s time to properly meet Fai.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45156611/91d04db4b90cb9412f90c7d5bc589c21ff1b515a.png

The World of Trip Space
We can't properly introduce our main character without telling you a bit about the world that Tempest Tower takes place in. The concept of Trip Space was originally created as a backdrop for our First-Person Puzzle game, Spectacle. It is a surreal, abstract collection of floating islands and strange vistas that living creatures visit while dreaming, or meditating, or... by other means. Visitors to Trip Space manifest as Peepers (cute little eyeball creatures with wings), they are able to observe this strange world, but they rely on the native Trip Tenders to properly shepherd them through their experience.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45156611/09438a86a69216c199f28f981792a87846d9d82c.gif

Living and visiting Trip Space was always tranquil, but the recent invasion of Creepers has turned the experience into a nightmare! An ominous dark fog has engulfed the many islands of Trip Space and it feels impossible to stand against the horde that emerges from it. This is when Tempest Tower takes place.

Who is Fai
Fai is a Trip Tender, a native inhabitant of Trip Space and a caretaker of the world. Fai is a bit of an underachiever and definitely didn’t volunteer for the role of hero, they are underprepared and easily distracted, but they are also the only Trip Tender around.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45156611/8ee6fba1f2d5f4acdf93cf36be7d96a4d598c700.png
With the player’s help, Fai will become a battle-hardened veteran, and an expert strategist. They will learn to build crazy contraptions as well as use the world of Trip Space against the invasive Creeper forces, and most importantly, they will save the many Peepers who still visit Trip Space.

Fun Fact: We used the name Fai, because it is pronounced similarly to the Danish word Fej, which means coward (and is also close to the word for sweep).

Early Concepts
The native inhabitants of Trip Space being lizard people was an idea that we carried over from Spectacle. We wanted to use the backdrop of Trip Space to embrace the world of conspiracy theories, so the native inhabitants had to be a cult-like group of lizards.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45156611/7b3baac439111167cf5eb0f0880b1d931be7cf83.png
One of the first mechanics we discussed for Tempest Tower was the ability for our main character to Gust/Push/Waft at objects and enemies in the game. This led to very early concepts of a janitor/caretaker character that used a broom to clean objects and create gusts. We loved the idea of a caretaker character who is forced to go above and beyond to protect their world.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45156611/3b36b562b79764b77b1e3a8a693795ba30f3e1a9.png
The idea of the broom becoming a multipurpose tool for building, painting, and digging came a bit later. The broom became such a key part of Fai’s silhouette that it didn’t make sense to see them use any other tools. Thankfully, the game is generally a bit goofy, so it doesn’t feel that strange to see a character digging up a plant with a floppy broom.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45156611/c9e4b0333f32bbd89b391560b4124e2d6474f210.png
Now, drawing a concept and designing a character is one thing but of course we had to translate it to 3D, which is often a lot easier said than done!

From 2D to 3D
We were lucky enough to already have a base model to work from. Even though Spectacle was a First-Person game, we did have an “out of body” mechanic that meant we had to model our main character so they could be seen from any angle. This meant we had a place to start, but Fai was very much their own lizard so there was still a lot to do. The yellow rubber gloves really pop alongside Fai’s purple cloak and the trashcan backpack was just for added bounce and style.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45156611/8ed4748c4d443b351ccdf8bdc80ed94024b48251.png
The bouncy animation style is a mix of talented animation work from the HPY team and the Boing Kit plugin for Unity. We gained a lot of experience with expressive movement while working on our previous game, Time on Frog Island, and that did not go to waste here.

To get the perfect look for Fai in game, we are using ramped lighting with a custom ramp texture. We are using an emissive texture to get Fai’s eyes to glow and applying a matcap texture to enhance the soft lighting. An occlusion map is used, mainly to remove indirect lighting from Fai’s face so that the hood/cap can look like they are having a bigger impact on the lighting.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45156611/b5f13dbefc0cce1cb9e1edc619ad8a8ae2d3def4.gif

Get Involved!
We will have a public Demo releasing very soon, so you will be able to try out the Tutorial plus a special expanded level that we built to show off the intended difficulty of the full game.
If soon is too far away and you happen to live in Copenhagen, you can play the Tempest Tower Demo next week at Tomorrow’s Awesome Game Showcase! We hope to see you there.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45156611/20d2b4c41ac06d4b6e4deace4f7bdf3839128108.png

notes.title: Early Access Announcement
notes.content:
We have a much shorter update this time, mainly aimed at catching you up on our plans with Tempest Tower. Starting from next year we will have more regular updates about the game in the run up to launch. We can't wait to tell you more!
We are excited to announce that Tempest Tower will be our first self-published game. We plan to launch the game into Steam Early Access during the first half of 2025 and work closely with our community to build a game we are all proud of.
Why Early Access?
For Tempest Tower, we plan to fully embrace the open development style. We want to develop a strong community around the game, and we feel that the best way to do this is by getting players involved early and allowing them to shape the project with us.
We don’t yet know what the future holds, but we expect Tempest Tower to remain in Early Access for around 9 months. We will use that time to add content, quality of life features, and new game modes. The game will launch on Early Access as a tight experience with all core mechanics present, we aim to have 2-3 hours of base gameplay with endless extra hours of experimenting with loadouts and high score hunting on top.
If you are interested in getting involved right now, I suggest joining our Discord server. It has been fairly quiet over the last 18 months, but that will be changing as we move into next year!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45156611/b5d636b1b5ca638cdf7b4427672a8f786084ae4d.png
Steam Page Update
We are making this announcement alongside a big face lift to our Steam page. We have updated our capsule art, logo, and screenshots as well as finalized our store text so it can be translated in the new year. We have worked alongside another game development studio called BitEgg to update our Capsule Art and we couldn't be happier with the results, they have perfectly captured the vibe of Tempest Tower and we think that the new art really stands out in the Steam store.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45156611/d304629eb5224a5ba1f70d3257a0a728fe75d430.jpg
More News Coming Soon!
We will be properly showing Tempest Tower in motion for the first time when we reveal our first look trailer in early January. This will be our first big marketing push for the game and it will coincide with more news about what to expect from us in the run up to the games launch. Until then, we hope you have a relaxing holiday and a good new year!

notes.title: DevBlog: Designing levels for Tempest Tower
notes.content:
Hello!
We are excited to post our first proper Dev Blog and give the community a glimpse of how the sausage is made. This news post is a shortened version of the latest Half Past Yellow blog post, which can be read in full here: https://halfpastyellow.com/blog/2024/10/30/Level-Design-in-Tempest-Tower.html


Learning from our previous game
An important aspect of the Tempest Tower project is our ability to move quickly with ideas. Because of this, the decision was made early on to use a similar camera angle and movement style to our previous game, Time on Frog Island. Making this decision early allowed us to come into the project with some basic level design rules and a good understanding of how traversal should feel.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45156611/e9001e867f581b74b96257427743b6a39ee1010a.jpg
Key level design tenets from ToFI:

The island gains height/verticality the further ‘north’ that the player travels
All designed/expected jumps in the game are possible with about 1 meter of leeway (the game is not built to be a hardcore platformer)
It is always clear when the player needs to jump (exposed rock visuals)
The camera angle makes height differences in the geometry are difficult to parse so take off points for ‘1-way jumps’ should be marked clearly
If the player is ever completely obscured by terrain (which was used sparingly), the ground should be completely smooth and require no jumps to pass through 


Blocking out a level
While we are lucky to be starting with so much knowledge from Time on Frog Island. It was still necessary to find the fun within Tempest Tower. The rules above gave us a good place to start, but we had to be fast at creating new levels so we could properly test different gameplay features. Blockouting a level always went through three stages of focus; player movement, enemy paths, gameplay objects/items.

The base terrain is built up by connecting and overlapping pre-built platform pieces in order to create flat open areas, terraced hillsides, and connecting slopes. Pre-built rock shapes are used to plug holes, block jumps, and add visual variety to the space. We are using a world space triplanar shader for both the ground material as well as the exposed rock material so that we can guarantee that the terrain textures always line up. This does generate quite a bit of overlapping geometry, which we might need to revisit at a later date, but it isn’t currently a performance problem.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45156611/9005eff383b7c9a1f8e4facf84e6b1d14a3bd6fd.png
Enemies cannot jump or drop off ledges (for now), so platforming areas act as shortcuts between different sections of the level. We always build levels with a player movement focus first as it has the largest impact on the fun factor of a level. Levels can often feel a little bare at this point, but understanding how the player moves around a level is important to understand before moving onto the next step.

Once we have a good first pass on the overall level, the focus shifts to building enemy paths. A level in Tempest Tower needs to feel amazing (and ideally different) to traverse during the Building Phase and the Action Phase. The route(s) that enemies take through the level can greatly affect the flow of the space, tight corridors become impassable while high cliffs can be more easily reached. Because of this, we are still making big changes to the base terrain while we decide how to weave enemy paths through it.

The final piece of the blockouting puzzle is the setup of game objects and items. These are gameplay relevant elements that the player can interact with and use during the level, (things like resource spawners, bombs, destructible blockers, etc.). Once added, the level is properly playable, and the designer can start to evaluate, refine and balance (which is where the real fun begins).

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45156611/8ade3eef21ea78e87812ca00221c09d4f91589b0.gif
Read more on our website!
If you enjoyed learning a bit about how we design levels for Tempest Tower, then you can continue this Dev Blog on our website.

The post goes on to describe some early gameplay failures and how changes to the game design impacted the types of levels that we created.
